section_summary: This section records U.S. debate over expanding Japanese fishing grounds and imposing conservation standards, alongside documents on Japan’s 1948–49 Antarctic whaling expedition. It also contains correspondence on U.S. approval of the Indo-Pacific Fisheries Council and an April 1948 FAO Fisheries Bulletin with the Baguio Agreement and international fisheries statistics.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on extending Japanese fishing rights
subfiles.about: Recommends support for Japanese fishing expansion while reserving Trust Territory access pending Army–Navy agreement.
subfiles.summary: Concludes that excluding Japan from the Trust Territory would undermine U.S. trade policy and cost Japan valuable food.

subfiles.title: Japanese Fishing
subfiles.about: Records Mr. Lovett’s decisions on the SANACC 99/8 compromise.
subfiles.summary: Lovett supported the compromise, urged caution on Trust Territory access, and called for Japanese conservation standards.

subfiles.title: Departure of Japanese Antarctic Whaling Expedition
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports the departure of two Japanese Antarctic whaling fleets and transmits three enclosures.
subfiles.summary: The fleets departed November 12 and 13 with SCAP supervisors and Australian and British observers.

subfiles.title: Two-Fleet Whaling Expedition Leaves Nov. 12, 13
subfiles.from: Public Information Office, General Headquarters, Far East Command
subfiles.about: Announces Japanese whaling-fleet departures, expected catch, vessels, managers, and Allied observers.
subfiles.summary: Lists the two fleets, their planned production, and the SCAP supervisors and Allied observers accompanying them.

subfiles.title: Japanese Whaling Operations in the Antarctic in the 1948–1949 Season
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Rules on three proposed amendments to the Japanese Antarctic whaling plan.
subfiles.summary: Approves the first two amendments and rejects the third.

subfiles.title: Explanation of SCAPIN 5822-A/5
subfiles.about: Explains approval of a substitute catcher boat and revised sailing schedule, and rejection of extra fuel.
subfiles.summary: The new boat improves efficiency and the schedule meets convention rules; additional fuel was deemed unjustified.

subfiles.title: Letter requesting Interior comment on SANACC 99/10
subfiles.about: Seeks Interior’s comment or concurrence on Army amendments to Japanese fishing policy.
subfiles.summary: The Army accepts earlier SANACC proposals subject to amendments in SANACC 99/10.

subfiles.title: SANACC 99/10: U.S. Policy for Japanese Fishing and Other Aquatic Industries
subfiles.about: Comments on Army proposals to accelerate and broaden Japanese fishing-area expansion.
subfiles.summary: Allison favors an immediate decision on southern expansion but regards SANACC 99/8 as a reasonable interim approach if agreement is unavailable. He accepts detailed SCAP assurances in place of formal proof of conservation compliance and suggests patrol-vessel observation.

subfiles.title: Proposed Directive to SCAP Concerning Fishing
subfiles.to: Mr. Keyes; Major Lieding; Mr. Chaney
subfiles.about: Circulates a draft communication to SCAP for review.
subfiles.summary: Requests telephone approval or a December 8 meeting if substantial changes are needed.

subfiles.title: Proposed Directive to SCAP—Fishing Activities
subfiles.about: Proposes conservation, research, conduct, and publicity standards for Japanese fishing.
subfiles.summary: Urges SCAP to teach Japanese fisheries international conservation and vessel practices, maintain scientific research, and publicize progress to reduce opposition to future fishing access.

subfiles.title: Conservation responsibilities for Japanese fishing operations
subfiles.about: Examines guidance to SCAP on conservation and management of Japanese aquatic activities.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum links prewar Japanese fishing practices to continuing international opposition. It recommends surveillance, adjustment of catches to sustain productivity, cooperation where nations share fishing grounds, and publicity on Japan’s progress.

subfiles.title: Proposed interdepartmental cable on Japanese fishing conservation
subfiles.from: Departments of State, Army, Navy, and Interior
subfiles.about: Sets out a proposed conservation and publicity program for Japanese fisheries.
subfiles.summary: Calls for surveillance, sustained yields, international cooperation, and publicity on Japanese practices.

subfiles.title: Explanation of proposed Japanese fisheries conservation program
subfiles.about: Explains Interior’s conservation concerns and submits a proposed SCAP program for SANACC approval.
subfiles.summary: A State–Army–Interior working group proposes surveillance, sustained productivity, cooperation with other nations, and public reporting. The program aims to improve Japanese fishing conduct and reduce opposition to expanded access.

subfiles.title: Proposed State–Army cable on Japanese fishing practices
subfiles.about: Proposes a fishing-conservation program and asks how much SCAP already carries out.
subfiles.summary: Requests comment on current practice and further action needed for the proposed program.

subfiles.title: Comments on Flory’s proposed directive to SCAP concerning fishing
subfiles.about: Reviews the form, timing, and wording of the proposed fisheries directive.
subfiles.summary: Bacon suggests waiting for agreement on SANACC 99/8 and considering a less formal instruction.

subfiles.title: Comments on SANACC 99/4
subfiles.about: Raises questions about Japanese fishing-area expansion and referral to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Urges careful review of West Coast fishing interests, conservation language, and likely FEC opposition.

subfiles.title: Reply on SANACC 99/4
subfiles.about: Answers concerns about the proposed fishing area and FEC handling.
subfiles.summary: Fearey says departmental fisheries officials approved the proposal and argues that Japan needs expanded western Pacific fishing grounds. Although SCAP could act without FEC approval, he considers FEC consideration politically useful and believes approval may be attainable.

subfiles.title: Handling of Attached Fishing Area Paper
subfiles.about: Discusses whether to seek FEC approval or rely on SCAP authority.
subfiles.summary: Recommends sounding out FEC representatives while retaining options for an interim directive.

subfiles.title: FE concurrence on Indo-Pacific Fisheries Council agreement
subfiles.about: Reports Far Eastern Affairs divisions’ agreement to U.S. approval of the Baguio Agreement.
subfiles.summary: Notes Interior’s approval and expects formal notification to FAO.

subfiles.title: Approval of the Baguio Agreement
subfiles.about: Requests objections to approving the agreement establishing the Indo-Pacific Fisheries Council.
subfiles.summary: Describes the council’s research and information functions. Bacon flags the broad geographic scope and a remote possibility of research involving the Trust Territory.

subfiles.title: Comment on approval of the Baguio Agreement
subfiles.about: Comments on U.S. approval of the Indo-Pacific Fisheries Council.
subfiles.summary: Supports approval because the United States proposed the council, while doubting rapid gains in fish supply.

subfiles.title: Routing note for FAO Fisheries Bulletin
subfiles.about: Draws attention to the Baguio Agreement within the attached bulletin.
subfiles.summary: Asks the reader to review the agreement and return the attachment.

subfiles.title: FAO Fisheries Bulletin No. 2
subfiles.about: Publishes the Baguio Agreement and international fisheries trade, landings, and country reports.
subfiles.summary: The bulletin prints the proposed Indo-Pacific Fisheries Council agreement, including its functions, membership, funding, amendment, and withdrawal rules. It compares prewar and postwar fisheries trade and landings across numerous countries, including Japan. Country reports describe Icelandic fishing, Venezuelan development efforts, Brazilian landings, and British production.
